title: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Fiji: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: Terminal Illness & End-of-Life Planning in Fiji: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step serious and terminal illness checklist for Fiji: palliative care coordination, advance directives, powers of attorney, disability and caregiver support, and estate preparation.
introHtml: Planning administrative, healthcare, financial, and estate matters in advance in Fiji reduces pressure on families and ensures critical legal documents match domestic statutory rules. Because Fiji legislation differs from jurisdictions that offer lasting health-care proxies or general death duties, advance arrangements should follow local statutes and institutional procedures [1][4][6][9].

steps.title: Healthcare coordination, palliative care, and statutory workplace leave
steps.html:
• Coordinate specialist hospital care, symptom relief, and community health referrals through Ministry of Health and Medical Services Fiji (158 toll-free enquiries; 911 emergency ambulance; divisional contacts in Central/Eastern, Western, and Northern divisions) [13].
  • Under the Employment Relations Act 2007, eligible employees are entitled to at least 10 working days of paid sick leave annually (s. 68) and 3 working days of paid bereavement leave (s. 69) [10]. Note that the Employment Relations (Amendment) Bill 2025 (Bill No. 27 of 2025) proposes updating section 25 on employee wage settlement rules and reinstating at least 3 working days of paid family care leave under section 68A, and remains under Parliamentary review rather than enacted law [10][11].
  • Discuss care preferences directly with the treating medical team and family members while the patient has full decision-making capacity, keeping signed clinical summaries accessible [13].

steps.title: Drafting or reviewing a Will and understanding Power of Attorney limits
steps.html:
• Prepare or review a valid written Will compliant with execution rules under the Wills Act (Cap. 59) so asset instructions are clear [1]. Under section 13 of the Wills Act (Cap. 59), marriage automatically revokes a prior will unless the will expressly states that it is made in contemplation of that marriage [1].
  • Clarify the legal limits of Powers of Attorney in Fiji: ordinary powers executed under the Powers of Attorney Act (Cap. 27) govern property and financial acts while the donor retains legal capacity, rather than operating as UK-style enduring health-and-welfare lasting powers once incapacity occurs [2]. Review real property ownership titles and joint-tenancy vs. tenancy-in-common holdings against the Property Law Act (Cap. 130) [3].
  • If institutional executor or trustee support is appropriate, review will drafting and estate administration options with Fiji Public Trustee Corporation Limited (FPTCL) or an admitted Fiji legal practitioner [1][4].

steps.title: Fiji National Provident Fund (FNPF) nominations, MOA, and medical withdrawal
steps.html:
• File and verify an up-to-date nomination with Fiji National Provident Fund (FNPF) through the member portal or Form FNPF 5 so FNPF knows who is designated to receive member savings, subject to statutory probate and beneficiary rules [5][6].
  • Ensure both an active Memorandum of Administration (MOA) and the annual Special Death Benefit (SDB) premium are kept current: under FNPF rules, the Special Death Benefit can provide up to FJD 8,500 alongside the account balance, while expedited Funeral Assistance (up to FJD 2,000 within roughly 20 working days) requires both a valid MOA on file and payment of that financial year's SDB premium [5][6].
  • Where serious medical conditions require early financial support or permanent cessation of work, review Medical Incapacity Withdrawal requirements (Form FW03) and partial or full withdrawal criteria on FNPF's official withdrawal pages [7][8].

steps.title: Vital civil documents, FNPF records, and tax readiness
steps.html:
• Verify spelling consistency across birth certificates, marriage certificates, passports, TIN cards, land titles, and bank records against records held by Ministry of Justice Fiji - BDM Registry [9]. Confirm current fees before ordering duplicate certified extracts [9].
  • Check tax filing compliance and TIN details with Fiji Revenue and Customs Service (FRCS) ((+679) 3243000 or 1326 toll-free in Fiji) so income tax returns, business registrations, or property transfer assessments are orderly [14]. Fiji does not levy inheritance or estate taxes, though income tax and capital gains obligations on asset transfers remain relevant [14].
  • Store original Deeds, titles, share certificates, and the original signed Will in a known, accessible safe location, because High Court probate practice requires original instruments rather than photocopies [4][9].

steps.title: Cross-border Apostille preparation and international family files
steps.html:
• If family members, banks, pensions, or real assets are located outside Fiji, prepare certified civil status documents and notarized authorizations early and confirm whether an Apostille is required by the destination country [12].
  • Fiji issues Apostilles under the 1961 Hague Convention through its Competent Authority, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs [12]. Verify destination translation rules so foreign institutions can process documents without delay [12].
  • Compile a written inventory covering Fiji and overseas bank accounts, FNPF numbers, insurance policies, safe deposit keys, and digital credentials for the named executor or trusted family member [4][5].

prefillQuestion: A family member is facing a serious or terminal illness in Fiji. We need an overview of the main official steps and contacts in Fiji for palliative care, powers of attorney, advance directives, and caregiver support.

contacts.name: Ministry of Health and Medical Services Fiji
contacts.note: Toll-free enquiries 158 (Monday-Friday 8:00-16:30); medical emergency ambulance 911; Central/Eastern (679) 332 0844, Western (679) 666 0411, Northern (679) 881 2522.

contacts.name: Fiji National Provident Fund (FNPF)
contacts.note: Handles member Nominations, Memorandum of Administration (MOA), Special Death Benefit premiums, and Medical Incapacity Withdrawals (Form FW03). Short code: 5857.

contacts.name: Ministry of Justice Fiji - BDM Registry
contacts.note: Issues certified Fiji birth, marriage, and death extracts required for identity alignment, FNPF nominations, and probate records.

contacts.name: Fiji Public Trustee Corporation Limited (FPTCL)
contacts.note: Public trustee providing will preparation, estate administration, and trustee guidance in Fiji.

contacts.name: Fiji Revenue and Customs Service (FRCS)
contacts.note: Tax administration for TIN status, final tax readiness, and property or business tax clearances. Toll-free line within Fiji: 1326.
